narrative: Demand for PL1__MC2D4B86 averages 4,363 units/day with moderate variability (CV=0.328) and a statistically significant decreasing trend over the observation window. Lead times are extremely short (mean 0.27 days) but highly volatile (CV=1.81), making lead-time variance the dominant uncertainty driver. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 57,600 units and a data-driven safety stock of 3,707 units is recommended, replacing the heavily oversized SAP safety stock of 50,370 units while maintaining the 95% service level target and respecting the 125,979-unit storage constraint.
warnings: Decreasing demand trend detected (p=0.017) — forecast should be reviewed periodically
Lead time CV=1.81 is very high; monitor supplier reliability closely
EOQ constrained to storage capacity; unconstrained EOQ was 57,648 units

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) Continuous Review with EOQ order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Moderate demand CV (0.328) and approximately normal distribution support classical EOQ-based replenishment. Continuous review is preferred over periodic review given the high lead-time variability (CV=1.81), ensuring the reorder point triggers replenishment before stockout risk materialises. MOQ of 25,185 is covered by the EOQ of 57,600.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 125,979 units mildly constrains the order quantity (unconstrained EOQ=57,648 vs. effective cap=122,272). Cap does not bind materially; peak inventory at 61,307 units represents 48.7% utilisation. If safety stock were set at the SAP level of 50,370, remaining storage would limit order quantity to 75,609 — still above MOQ.
